items.title: Hospitalization Count from Mississauga Apartment Fire Climbs to 18, CBC Reports
items.summary: CBC Toronto reports that the number of people hospitalized after Monday's fire at a Mississauga apartment building near Inverhouse Drive and Lakeshore Road West has climbed to at least 18, including a firefighter and a Peel police officer. According to CBC, residents of the building were left shaken by the blaze, which broke out in a hallway and forced an evacuation. Peel Regional Police say the fire may have been arson, though investigators had not confirmed a cause as of Monday. The higher count marks an increase from earlier same-day estimates that had put the number of people treated closer to 10 or 11, suggesting more people were assessed for smoke inhalation and other injuries as the day went on. The officer and firefighter who were hurt were both injured while helping other residents get safely out of the building.

items.title: Councillors Call E-Scooters a Safety 'Crisis' as Mississauga Lobbies Queen's Park for Tighter Rules
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga officials have escalated their push for the provincial government to tighten regulations on e-scooters, with one city councillor describing the current situation around the motorized devices as a public safety crisis. Mayor Carolyn Parrish said she expects Ontario's transportation minister, Prabmeet Sarkaria, may soon announce that police across the province will get expanded authority to enforce road rules against e-scooter riders. The provincial government is expected to address e-scooters and e-bikes more broadly, with new regulations anticipated sometime this fall. Parrish and Ward 3 Councillor Chris Fonseca were part of a Mississauga delegation that raised e-scooter safety directly with provincial officials last month at the Association of Municipalities of Ontario conference in Ottawa. The city followed up after that conference with letters to the province spelling out its concerns and requests on several fronts. Parrish told council last Wednesday that the Ottawa trip was really productive and that provincial ministers and other officials listened to the city on several fronts, including on e-scooter safety.

items.title: Sixth Annual Gathering and Healing Weekend Brings Indigenous Art and Ceremony Back to Mississauga
items.summary: According to organizer Eagle Spirits of the Great Waters, the sixth annual Gathering and Healing Weekend and Art Mashkiki Indigenous Art Exhibit returns to the Small Arms Inspection Building in Mississauga from September 25 to 27. The free, public event is open to people of all ages and includes dance, music, storytelling, art, an Indigenous market, food and ceremony meant to share First Nations, Metis and Inuit arts and cultures. Eagle Spirits of the Great Waters is a Mississauga-based, Indigenous-led non-profit that runs the annual weekend in connection with the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, observed each year on September 30 alongside Orange Shirt Day. Both days are dedicated to honouring Residential School survivors, their families and communities, and to recognizing the lasting impact of Canada's residential school system. The organization says the weekend creates a space for Indigenous and non-Indigenous people to come together through culture, art, learning, remembrance and healing. Opening night on Friday features Indigenous artists and vendors, light refreshments, welcoming remarks, drumming from Eagle Spirits, and live music from Dwayne Laforme and the Boogie Blues Band.

items.title: Union Says Trucks Keep Going Out of Service as Mississauga Firefighter Staffing Strains Grow
items.summary: The Mississauga Fire Fighters Association, IAFF Local 1212, says daily staffing shortages have repeatedly forced Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services to pull trucks out of service since August, while the city maintains that emergency response coverage has not been compromised. According to the union, its first public post flagged six trucks out of service on August 22 across Wards 3, 5, 7 and 9, and it has continued posting regular updates since, with its most recent post on September 17 reporting three trucks out of service. The union says the city had 30 front-line fire trucks two decades ago and now has 33, even as Mississauga's population has grown by nearly 100,000 people alongside more highrises, more traffic and more emergencies. The union wrote in one of its posts that this isn't progress, it's reduced protection, and asked whether residents consider that safe. The union argues Mississauga residents deserve to know when front-line emergency response capacity is being reduced. City officials, for their part, say staffing pressures exist but that emergency response coverage has been maintained throughout.

items.title: Three Mississauga Police Divisions Accounted for Most of Peel's Hate Crime Reports Last Year
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police's 2025 Annual Hate-Motivated Crime Report, released in June 2026, hate-motivated crimes across Brampton and Mississauga rose 17 per cent to 195 incidents in 2025, up from 166 in 2024. The report shows Mississauga's three police divisions accounted for 136 of those 195 incidents, or nearly 70 per cent of all hate crimes recorded across both cities. Race, ethnicity and nationality were the most common motivating factors, cited in 146 of the 195 incidents, up from 98 such incidents in 2024. The report follows Peel police shifting investigative responsibility for hate-motivated crimes to a dedicated Hate Crime Unit in July 2025. Peel's population is heavily made up of visible minorities, with more than 69 per cent of residents identifying as South Asian, Black, Chinese, Filipino or Arab according to the 2021 census, a demographic backdrop the report cites in its data.

items.title: Burnhamthorpe Road Tops Mississauga's List of Dangerous Driving Complaints So Far This Year
items.summary: Statistics set to go before Mississauga's Road Safety Committee show Peel Regional Police received 476 Road Watch reports of careless or aggressive driving in the city between January 1 and July 31, 2026, with careless driving and speeding topping the list of alleged violations. According to the Road Watch data, Burnhamthorpe Road drew more reports than any other street in the city, with 20 complaints, followed by Mississauga Road and Winston Churchill Boulevard with 17 each and Dixie Road with 16. Road Watch is a community-driven program that lets residents report dangerous or aggressive drivers directly to police. Burnhamthorpe Road is one of the city's longest streets, running from Mississauga's western boundary all the way to its eastern border with Toronto, which helps explain why it draws the most reports. Peel police told the Road Safety Committee in January that Road Watch numbers help officers identify which roads, and which specific sections of them, might need additional patrols.

items.title: Yom Kippur Prompts Extra Peel Police Patrols at Mississauga, Brampton Synagogues After Belleville Shooting
items.summary: Peel police say they have stepped up patrols around places of worship and cultural centres in Mississauga and Brampton after a shooting outside a synagogue in Belleville on Sunday night. According to police in Belleville, an officer came across an individual near Bleecker Avenue and Victoria Avenue, a mostly residential part of the city located about 180 kilometres east of Toronto, and an altercation left both the officer and the individual injured and taken to hospital. The incident happened near the Sons of Jacob Synagogue during a gathering to mark Yom Kippur. Ontario's Special Investigations Unit, which is automatically called in whenever a police interaction with the public results in serious injury, has been notified and is now involved. Belleville police say they are not providing further comment while that investigation proceeds. Peel police added that through the High Holidays period, including Yom Kippur, they have increased their presence around synagogues and cultural centres across Mississauga and Brampton as a precaution.

items.title: Rescue Effort at Burning Mississauga Apartment Leaves Officer and Firefighter Injured
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say an officer and a firefighter were both hurt early Monday morning while helping residents escape a fire at an apartment building near Inverhouse Drive and Lakeshore Road West. According to police, crews responded to the blaze, which broke out in a hallway, and found several people trapped inside suffering from smoke inhalation. Acting Sgt. Amanda Steenson told reporters that one of the officers was hurt while helping a firefighter pull a resident from the building during the rescue. Ten people were taken to hospital by ambulance as a result of the fire. The cause has not yet been determined, and police say an investigation into what sparked the blaze is underway. Steenson said investigators could release suspect information later if the fire is found to have been deliberately set.

items.title: City Marks National Tree Day by Touting Progress Toward Its One Million Trees Goal
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says it is marking National Tree Day on September 23, part of National Forest Week, as a reminder of the role trees play in city life and in helping urban areas adapt to climate change. According to the city, trees clean the air, support biodiversity, and act as natural air conditioners that help keep neighbourhoods and buildings cooler as extreme weather becomes more common. The city says it is continuing to work toward its goal of planting one million trees by 2032, with 653,729 trees planted so far. Volunteers continue to plant trees and take part in stewardship activities that expand the city's urban forest and green spaces, according to the city. Officials say trees planted near watercourses and waterbodies are especially valuable, since they help with flood mitigation in addition to supporting biodiversity. The city is inviting residents to mark the day by getting outside and is highlighting its Forestry Fall Festival as one way to do that.
